safety_lead_time.comparison_action: INCREASE by 1.40 days — SAP value of 2.0 days is insufficient given unstable lead times

narrative: Material PL1__M957146C exhibits lumpy intermittent demand (CV=1.52, 54% active days) with a mild declining trend of -1.71 units/day over the observation window. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.734, mean=1.40 days), warranting an increase in safety lead time from the current SAP value of 2.0 to 3.4 days. The (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity (capped to 2,807 by storage capacity) reduces annual cost by 15.1% while maintaining 95% service level, primarily through a 55.4% reduction in safety stock.
warnings: Storage capacity is fully utilised at peak replenishment: SS(486) + OQ(2807) = 3293 ≈ max_storage_units(3293.62). Any upward revision of safety stock requires additional storage.
Order quantity was capacity-constrained from unconstrained EOQ of 2887 to 2807 units.
Declining demand trend detected (-1.71 units/day) — annual demand estimate may overstate future requirements.

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) — Continuous-review reorder-point with fixed EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy intermittent demand with high lead-time variability (CV=0.734) requires a continuous-review policy that triggers replenishment as soon as inventory hits the reorder point, rather than a periodic review which would accumulate additional demand uncertainty. The EOQ order quantity minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs under the observed annual demand of ~35,777 units.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is fully consumed at peak (SS+OQ=3,293 vs limit=3,293.62). A 1-unit increase in safety stock would require reducing order quantity below the EOQ optimum. If demand volatility increases, the safety stock formula will recommend higher SS, creating a binding capacity conflict that cannot be resolved without expanding storage.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ(136)+SS(486)=622 is well below max_storage_units(3293.62); no MOQ-capacity infeasibility exists.
